_source: registry.d/arch-declarations.json — declares `arch` on the thirteen shipped Flatpak entries that carried `arch: null`, staged 2026-08-19 for merge into registry.json under `apps`. These are EDITS to entries that already exist, not new apps: merge replaces them.
_why: An entry with no `arch` is an UNVERIFIED CLAIM TO EVERY ARCHITECTURE. ArchSupported permits it, the box offers it, and on the wrong architecture the install fails after the download. All thirteen turn out to publish both arches, so nothing is lost by saying so and the App Hub stops guessing.
_ratchet: MERGING THIS FIRES backend/services/appnet/arch_test.go's ratchet, BY DESIGN AND IN THE GOOD DIRECTION. undeclaredArchCeiling is 19, transcribed from a measurement. After this merge the count is 6 (diagrams-net, excalidraw, hoppscotch, immich, uptime-kuma, vaultwarden — all `_disabled`, none installable), and TestRegistry_UndeclaredArchOnlyEverFalls FAILS with 'below the ceiling — lower it to 6', which is the test refusing to let its own bound go slack. Set undeclaredArchCeiling = 6 in the SAME commit that merges this. That is the ratchet TIGHTENING; it is not the anti-shrinkage relaxation the standing rule forbids, and this agent deliberately did not make the edit itself.
_signing: UNSIGNED BY CONSTRUCTION: every entry carries "signature": "". Run `make sign-registry` then `make verify-registry-prod` after merging.
_verified_by: Flathub API v2 (summary + appstream + verification) 2026-08-19, plus scripts/verify-flatpak-candidates.sh --file registry.d/arch-declarations.json, which resolves each id through a real `flatpak remote-info` per declared architecture.

audacity._note: ARCH DECLARED 2026-08-19, measured not guessed. This entry shipped with `arch: null`, which ArchSupported reads as an unverified claim to EVERY architecture Vulos builds. Flathub publishes org.audacityteam.Audacity for ['amd64', 'arm64'] (API v2 summary, confirmed by `flatpak remote-info flathub --arch=` for each). Both arches, so the app follows a user onto either instance unchanged — the standing directive that every instance is near a clone of the next, satisfied with no emulation. SIGNATURE CLEARED: any byte changed after signing invalidates that entry's signature, so leaving the old one would produce a verdict of `Publisher signature did not verify` — strictly worse than unsigned. It re-signs with the rest at the ceremony.
